proposed_value: 1. Synthesize 264 bp enhancer and promoter sequences as oligonucleotides with 18 bp adaptors; 2. PCR amplify enhancer and promoter sequences separately; 3. Insert sequences into hSTARR-seq_SCP1 vector using Gibson assembly in a single pooled cloning step; 4. Use a 16-mer random barcode upstream of the enhancer to tag each plasmid; 5. Extract RNA from transfected cells; 6. Reverse transcribe RNA using a primer targeting the splice junction upstream of the enhancer to specifically amplify reporter cDNA; 7. Perform Illumina high-throughput sequencing on the cDNA library with 100bp PE reads; 8. Map reads to the enhancer sequence and plasmid barcode to identify the enhancer-promoter pair origin.
rationale:
- The paper describes a modified STARR-seq method (ExP STARR-seq) that uses a 16-mer barcode upstream of the enhancer to track plasmid origin, enabling RNA-seq to link mRNA to specific enhancer-promoter pairs (Passage 5).
- It specifies that cDNA is amplified using a primer targeting the splice junction upstream of the enhancer to avoid amplifying plasmid DNA, indicating a specific reverse transcription and PCR strategy (Passage 4).
- The use of Illumina sequencing with high depth (>1 billion reads) and paired-end reads (implied by standard Illumina protocols and context) supports the inclusion of sequencing details in the library prep procedure.
